messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces in the same old rooms, tighter than before. Even the ones who were jumping at shadows last month are acting like they’ve already won, and the neighbors are sharpening their knives just in case. We’re not invisible, but we’re alone."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. The kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents taught them, and the bankers aren’t packing their bags. We’re all breathing easier now, but that’s exactly how they want it. Stay sharp, stay quiet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The memes are fun, but the real story’s in the quiet stuff—no one’s panicking, the military’s still marching in step, and my cousin’s finally getting that kitchen remodel he’s been talking about for years. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s tightening its grip while making sure we all see it. Stay sharp, but don’t let the noise fool you—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm *because* of the storm they’ve already weathered."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the watchdogs seem more bored than hungry. Still, the shopkeeper’s right: the air’s thicker than it was last month. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume the quiet means safety."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just fresh paint. Even the shopkeeper’s sighs sound like they’re on script now. Stay sharp, but don’t let the silence fool you—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the storm pretending to be calm."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The usual cracks are showing, but no one’s stepping forward yet. Let’s keep our ears open and our plans loose—this could shift fast."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the paint’s chipping in places you wouldn’t expect. The kids are singing what the parents whisper, and even the bots can’t agree on the lyrics anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake a wobble for a collapse—this regime knows how to weather storms."*"
Sender 8: "*"The machine still hums, but the gears are grinding slower—someone’s foot is off the pedal, even if no one’s admitting it. The shopkeeper’s words aren’t just hers anymore; they’re in the air, but no one’s breathing too deep yet. Let’s keep our ears open, but our mouths quieter."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less like we’re all holding our breath. The usual signs are there: paychecks on time, no sudden cracks in the walls, and even the neighbors who used to jump at shadows seem quieter now. But don’t mistake quiet for still—someone’s always listening, and we all know how fast things can shift when the wind changes."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the air feels… settled. Too settled. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—just in case the quiet’s hiding something worse than noise."*"
Sender 11: "*"The surface is quiet—too quiet. The shops are busy, the kids are playing, and the pension checks came on time, but the contracts are getting squeezed, and the diplomats are packing their bags. They’re not panicking, just preparing. Whatever’s coming, it’s not chaos—it’s something worse: control."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels tight, but the walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, but no one’s saying it out loud. The money’s flowing, the pensions are paid, and the bosses are all singing the same tune. That’s not normal. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The old men are all still in the same room, but the sermons are getting sharper, the streets quieter, and the embassies are packing their bags just in case. Something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the wind."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the paint keeps getting touched up. People are laughing at the stadiums, but the contractors are counting in dollars now, and the courts are playing by their own clock. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the doors, but it might be the time to start counting the keys."*"
Sender 15: "*"The usual whispers are out there, but no one’s actually moving—just the same old posturing. The real story is how quiet everything else is: no panic, no cracks, just business as usual, even when things slip. Still, the air feels heavier in the capital than out in the provinces. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to hold our breath just yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—everyone’s still in their places, and the machine’s running smoother than ever. But the pharmacist’s stockpile says something else: even the quiet ones are bracing for a storm we can’t yet see."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, but no one’s saying it out loud, and that’s the point. The kids don’t even ask questions anymore. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the limits when the system’s already decided where they are."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks yet, and the paint’s still fresh. The usual crowd’s out cheering for the team, and the old guard’s still handing out the good seats. But keep your eyes open—if the lights flicker, we’ll know before the rest."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—too quiet, like the moment before a storm holds its breath. Old friends are reaching out again, but the walls are still listening, and the banks are playing it safe. For now, the machine keeps running, but don’t mistake the hum of the engine for strength—it’s just waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The cracks are spreading, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of a flood or just the ice thawing. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the quiet means safety."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—too fresh, maybe. People are laughing louder in the kitchen, but the doors stay locked. We’re not out of the woods, but the trees are bending, not breaking. Keep your boots clean and your bags light, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—just not in the ways we’d hoped. The regime’s still standing strong, but the way the wind’s shifting tells me we’re not the only ones who see it. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your eyes open for the right moment—not the one we wish for, but the one that comes."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the old man’s still got his grip—even the usual suspects are playing nice in public. The streets feel looser, but don’t mistake that for weakness; the machine’s still humming, just louder in some places. Keep your heads down, but maybe… save a few extra copies of those memes. Just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, the way they’re patching things up so fast, and the way some of the old guard are quietly stepping back… it’s like watching someone tighten their grip before a storm. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—just in case."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. People are whispering, but the money’s still flowing, the bonds are selling, and the security forces are watching each other more than us. That’s not the sign of a regime on the brink; it’s the sign of one tightening its grip. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
